binders: An arbitrary type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A measure μ on Ω equipped with an IsProbabilityMeasure μ instance.
Two extended nonnegative-real exponents p and q.
hypotheses: p ≤ q in the standard partial order on extended nonnegative reals.
X is almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to μ; explicitly, X agrees μ-almost everywhere with some strongly measurable real-valued function.
conclusions: The extended Lp seminorm of X at exponent p is at most its extended Lq seminorm at exponent q: eLpNorm X p μ ≤ eLpNorm X q μ.
mathematical_definitions: ENNReal is WithTop NNReal, representing nonnegative-real values together with ∞.
For exponent 0, eLpNorm is defined as 0; for exponent ∞, it is an essential-supremum norm; for any other exponent r, it is eLpNorm' X r.toReal μ.
Almost-everywhere strong measurability means existence of a strongly measurable representative equal to X μ-almost everywhere.
The real topology used for measurability is induced from the pseudometric d(x,y)=|x-y|, and the real norm used by eLpNorm is supplied through the displayed normed-structure chain.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every measurable space Ω, every measure μ satisfying the supplied probability-measure typeclass condition, every real-valued function X on Ω, and every pair of extended nonnegative exponents p and q, if p is nonzero, p ≤ q, and X is almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to μ, then the extended Lp seminorm of X is no greater than its extended Lq seminorm.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The result applies only under the IsProbabilityMeasure μ instance; the dossier does not unfold the exact normalization condition encoded by that predicate.
The function is restricted to be Real-valued and almost everywhere strongly measurable.
The lower exponent p must be nonzero and must satisfy p ≤ q; data failing any premise impose no norm-comparison obligation because the proposition is an implication.
Because p is nonzero and p ≤ q in ENNReal, q cannot be zero, although this is not stated as a separate hypothesis.
Both exponents are extended nonnegative reals, so p or q may equal ∞; eLpNorm then uses its essential-supremum branch.
No finiteness or integrability hypothesis is imposed. Either norm may be ∞, and when the right-hand norm is ∞ the concluding inequality is automatically true in ENNReal.
The target compares seminorm values of functions directly and does not quantify over equivalence classes modulo almost-everywhere equality.
ambiguities: The defining fields or constructors of IsProbabilityMeasure are absent, so the exact proposition imposed on μ—although evidently intended as the probability-measure condition—cannot be verified from the packet alone.

The finite-exponent auxiliary eLpNorm' and infinite-exponent auxiliary eLpNormEssSup are referenced but not defined, so their exact normalization conventions cannot be reconstructed from this dossier.

NNNorm.toENorm and the source of Real's norm field are not unfolded, so the packet does not independently expose the exact pointwise extended norm, despite the surrounding declarations indicating the standard norm on Real.
